body:
Emily Stone: seeing another console vs invoice mismatch that looks like rounding. Example from Jan invoice preview for Acct #10421: console Usage page shows **1,234,567 output tokens** for 1/1–1/31, but invoice line item is **1,234,580 output tokens**. That’s +13 tokens. Customer already asked why totals don’t match.

Rishi Malhotra: +1 we need a crisp explanation here. Is this still per-request rounding somewhere? Or timezone boundary?

Chloe Martin: console currently rounds and displays at the *daily bucket* level (and we aggregate those in UI). invoice aggregator rounds only at invoice-run level (I think). If each day rounds up/down separately, could explain a handful of tokens.

Logan Wright: pulled a quick check from telemetry aggregates. For that account, raw sum (unrounded) output_tokens for Jan is **1,234,579.6**. If invoice rounds once at the end => **1,234,580**.

Logan Wright: console path (today) is doing `ROUND()` in the daily query, then summing days. Some days round down so you can end up at **1,234,567** depending on fractional carry.

Emily Stone: ok that matches the symptom. But why are we getting fractional tokens at all? tokens should be ints.

Nadia Rahman: tokens are ints at event-level, but we get fractional totals once we apply allocation/weighting for certain internal joins (e.g., when we attribute streamed chunks to request_id + retry merge and then aggregate by model alias). There’s a `SAFE_DIVIDE` in one of the intermediate views for “shared batch” accounting that can create decimals in the intermediate table.

Cole Summers: also note: cached token adjustments come in as deltas in the billing-ready table. Those are ints, but when we compute “effective billed tokens” for certain endpoints we apply a multiplier (legacy) for rerank normalization. That multiplier is being phased out but still exists in console query.

Rishi Malhotra: can we point to a doc / ADR so Finance & Support have something canonical? This keeps coming up.

Logan Wright: ADR draft exists (still in review): <https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ARCH/ADR-027+Meter+rounding+and+streaming+accounting|ADR-027 meter rounding + streaming accounting>.

Logan Wright: TL;DR proposal in ADR: **do not round per-request or per-day**. Only round once per invoice aggregation window, after all transformations. That’s what invoice code is supposed to do.

Chloe Martin: console is lagging behind ADR decision. It’s effectively doing “round per day” because the UI query is `GROUP BY day` and rounds before the sum. That’s the mismatch.

Emily Stone: what should we tell Support meanwhile? They’re going to get tickets like “invoice higher than console by ~0.001%”.

Allison Grant: we should treat console as *informational estimate* until alignment lands. But we need consistent wording + a link. Also: can we add a banner in console usage page?

Laura Bennett: agree on banner + canonical definition. For invoices we need auditability: invoice total is source-of-truth, console should converge to that.

Rishi Malhotra: can we craft an example explanation with numbers? Something simple.

Logan Wright: example:
- Raw (post-transform) output tokens = 1,234,579.6
- Invoice rounding rule = round at end of window => 1,234,580
- Console today = round per day, then sum => can be 1,234,567 depending on distribution of fractional parts by day
This isn’t “extra usage,” it’s rounding location.

Emily Stone: got it. But 13 tokens delta feels weirdly large for rounding location. Is that plausible?

Nadia Rahman: if you have ~31 daily buckets each with ~0.4–0.6 fractional carry, the diff can be up to ~15–20 tokens worst case (sum of daily round-downs vs final round). So +13 is plausible.

Chloe Martin: I can open a task to change console query to match invoice aggregation: sum raw unrounded across full window first, then apply the same rounding function. Also need to align timezone (console uses user locale today; invoice uses UTC month boundaries).

Cole Summers: FYI invoice aggregator PR in flight removes per-request rounding entirely (there was a leftover `ceil()` on a per-request field in one path). If that lands, we should ensure console uses same meter_version. Otherwise we’ll keep chasing.

Emily Stone: action items?

Chloe Martin: 1) I’ll draft console fix plan + add temporary banner copy. 2) Logan/Nadia can confirm where decimals introduced so we can document.

Logan Wright: I’ll add a snippet to ADR-027 with the explicit formula + example. Also will comment in #support-runbook with a short talk track.

Laura Bennett: please include in talk track: “Invoice is computed from billing-ready telemetry using the published rounding policy; console may differ while we roll out alignment.” No over-promising.

Rishi Malhotra: can we also add a control for month-end close: “console vs invoice delta expected within X tokens / X%” so Finance doesn’t panic each cycle.

Emily Stone: yes, but we should define tolerance. For now, if it’s purely rounding location, it should be tiny.

Allison Grant: we can add an alert only when delta > 0.5% or absolute > 5k tokens, otherwise ignore. (will reduce false positives)

Nadia Rahman: +1. Most real issues we’ve seen are 2–10% (streaming disconnect bug / retries). Rounding should be <0.01%.

Emily Stone: ok. For this account, we won’t hold invoice. I’ll respond to Support with the example + ADR link.

Chloe Martin: dropping suggested banner copy here:
`Usage totals in Console are being updated to match invoice aggregation (rounding + time window). Minor differences may occur during rollout. Invoices remain the source of truth.`

Logan Wright: works. I’ll also add a note: “UTC month boundary used for invoicing” so folks stop comparing local midnight.

Emily Stone: thanks all. Please ping when console fix is ready so we can close the loop on ongoing tickets.
